_provenance: Boston housing spatial-lag data. Source: the `boston` data of the R package spData (github.com/Nowosad/spData, data/boston.rda): `boston.c`, the 506-tract Harrison & Rubinfeld (1978) table with Gilley & Pace's corrected median value CMEDV, and `boston.soi`, the sphere-of-influence neighbours list for those tracts (spdep `nb`, symmetric, 1076 undirected edges, degrees 1-8). Response y = log(CMEDV); regressors are the Harrison & Rubinfeld hedonic set used in spdep's Boston examples (CRIM, ZN, INDUS, CHAS, NOX^2, RM^2, AGE, log(DIS), log(RAD), TAX, PTRATIO, B, log(LSTAT)), z-scored, with an intercept prepended. Two fixed weight matrices, both data: W = D^-1 B is the row-standardised contiguity and is the lag operator of the model equation (the convention the Boston SAR literature reports rho in); Ws = D^-1/2 B D^-1/2 is the symmetric normalised adjacency, similar to W and therefore of identical spectrum, used for the log-determinant so that it can be taken as a Cholesky of a symmetric positive definite matrix (Ord 1975; spdep's `similar.listw`). The identity log|I - rho W| = log|I - rho Ws| was checked over the stationary interval to 1.71e-13. eig(Ws) = [-0.970864, 1.000000], so the stationary interval is rho in (-1.0300, 1). Nothing is simulated: y and X are the recorded values. Built by benchmark/probprog/ablation/sicm_roster/build_boston_sar.py.
